I am 58 years old. I finished middle school and have been farming my own land for 30 years. My farm is 19.1 mu, which around Quzhou is a fairly large plot. I have 16 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 3.1 mu in cotton. Three people live in my house — me, my wife, and my son who works in the city but comes back for busy seasons.

I always start from what I did last year. Last year my wheat made about 470 jin per mu and my maize about 500 jin per mu. Fertilizer prices dropped a bit this spring compared to last year, so I will push my inputs up slightly on the wheat and maize because those two are where my real money comes from. Cotton is just 3.1 mu, more for household cash padding, but I still treat it seriously.

For the 16 mu of winter wheat: I sowed improved wheat seed last October, about 25 jin per mu. The wheat is greening up now. I already gave it one winter irrigation because the soil was dry. I will irrigate three more times — at jointing, at heading, and at grain filling. That is four irrigations total. For fertilizer, before sowing I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, 100 jin per mu of 15-15-15. Then at green-up I will spread 40 jin of urea per mu, and at jointing another 20 jin of urea per mu. Counting it up, that is roughly 16 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I do rotary tillage for wheat. I spray pesticide three times: herbicide now at green-up, then fungicide and insecticide together at heading, and one more insecticide spray if I see armyworms. I expect 480 kg per mu if the weather does not turn bad.

For the 16 mu of summer maize: After wheat harvest in early June, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed directly into the wheat stubble without plowing. You have only about ten days between harvest and sowing, so no-tillage saves me. I use about 3 jin of seed per mu. At sowing I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu — I use a high-nitrogen compound, 20-10-10. Then at big trumpet stage I topdress with 40 jin of urea per mu. That comes to about 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: right after sowing to help emergence, at jointing, and at grain filling. Pesticide is three times: a closed herbicide at sowing, then two sprays for corn borer and aphids. I expect 530 kg per mu.

For the 3.1 mu of cotton: I plant hybrid cotton seed in late April, about 2 jin per mu. I do rotary tillage in spring and put down farmyard manure plus 60 jin of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu. I topdress twice with urea, 15 jin each time. Total nutrients are about 13 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Cotton gets five pesticide sprays because bollworm, aphids, and mites all hit cotton hard here. I irrigate twice: at flowering and at boll stage. I expect 260 kg per mu of seed cotton.

I watch my neighbors. Old Wang across the road put 40 jin of urea on his wheat at green-up last year and his crop looked strong. If everyone around me is putting similar amounts, I do the same — I would rather spend an extra 50 yuan per mu on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost. But I do not go crazy because I have to think about my whole budget. My son sent home some money, but electricity for the well pump costs me 30 to 40 yuan per mu per irrigation. On 19.1 mu, every decision connects. Wheat and maize are my main crops, so they get first priority on money and labor.
